data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word nikos, meaning 'victory' or 'conqueror'. In the Bible, the name Nicolas is mentioned in Acts 6:5, as one of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles to serve the Greek-speaking community in Jerusalem. The name became popular in the Christian world due to this biblical reference. The name Nicol carries the meaning “Conquerer of the people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Nicol usually hope their child will grow to embody conquerer of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: ניקול
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ניקול הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'נצחון העם' או 'נוער לנצח'. השם ניקול הוא גרסה שונה של השם ניקולאוס, המורכב מהמילים היווניות 'ניק' (נצחון) ו'לאוס' (עם). השם ניקול מופיע בתנךך לא באופן ישיר, אך השם ניקולאוס מוזכר בברית החדשה, וישוע ניקולאי היה אחד מתלמידיו של ישו.

in_greek.name: Νικόλ
in_greek.meaning: Νικόλ - Νίκη του λαού, νίκη αιώνια
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Νικόλ προέρχεται από το ελληνικό όνομα Νικόλαος, που σημαίνει 'νίκη του λαού' ή 'αιώνια νίκη'. Το όνομα αποτελείται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'νίκη' (νίκη) και 'λαός' (λαός). Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Νικόλαος αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους επτά διακονους της πρώτης εκκλησίας της Ιερουσαλήμ.

in_latin.name: Nicol
in_latin.long_meaning: Nicol, derived from Nicolaus, means 'victory of the people' or 'eternal victory'. The name consists of the Latinized Greek words 'nike' (victory) and 'laos' (people). In early Christian tradition, the name Nicolai or Nicolaus was significant, associated with Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop known for his generosity.

in_english.name: Nicol
in_english.meaning: Victory of the people, eternal triumph, or conqueror of the nation
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nicol, a variant of Nicholas, originates from the Greek name Nikolaos (Νικόλαος), meaning 'victory of the people' or 'eternal triumph'. It is derived from the Greek words 'nike' (victory) and 'laos' (people). Although Nicol is not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name Nicholas appears in the New Testament (Acts 6:5), referring to one of the early deacons of the Church in Jerusalem. Historically, the name has been associated with Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop of Myra, known for his piety and generosity, especially towards children.
